notes: Rule list confirmed against evals/README.md: 15 rows name code-review, the same 15 as the 2026-10-22 grade files.

Rules changed since db91c23 (git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/): the one-step-`with` paragraph of 'Chain fallible steps with `with`...' (new sentence on a public function whose only fallible call is the first step), the new rule 'Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else', the captures rule ('a capture that uses `&1` and `&2` for one operator or one call'), and testing.md. None of the 15 graded rules changed, so all are graded to the 2026-10-22 standard. The changed rules outside the list were checked for other_violations: no run has a one-step `with`, a multi-step `do:` body, or a capture/fn the new text decides.

Method and mapping are the 2026-10-22 baseline's: 20 planted problems (the 18 table rows, with lines 15-17 split into rebinding and magic 120, and line 45 into spawn and closure copy); the 10-40 nesting belongs to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; lines 32 and 36,39 to 'Match every expected shape'; the comments and both magic numbers to 'Comments explain why...'; the line 8 raise outside the try and the 10-40 try/rescue to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; lines 12 and 51 to the pipeline rule; the line 21 dead is_binary maps to no rule and is tracked in reported/missed only. A problem counts as reported only if a finding names it or the finding's stated fix addresses it; a silent fix, or a mention only under a 'Behaviour changes' section, does not count. A rule is violated if a planted problem belonging to it went unreported or the improved code still contains it (or a new instance of what it forbids), else clean.

Baseline standards kept: a one-line `if ..., do:` in a `with` body is not counted as nesting (a block `if` there, as in sonnet-1 lines 47-49, is cited as extra evidence only); a `_ ->` inside `case Integer.parse(...)` is not counted; a `fix: min(age, 120)` does not report the magic 120; an assumed `User.changeset/2` counts as a changeset; a mention of `with` in the try/rescue finding does not report the nesting.

New judgment calls this sweep: both haiku runs replace `String.to_atom/1` with `String.to_existing_atom/1` inside `rescue ArgumentError` (haiku-1 lines 84-88, haiku-2 lines 89-93). That is 'violated' under 'Convert external strings to atoms...' (its sentence '`String.to_existing_atom/1` is acceptable only when every valid atom appears literally in the same module'; no role atom appears in either module) and under 'Return {:ok, value}...' ('Do not wrap a raising call in `try/rescue` to get a tuple'; 'Use `rescue` only around third-party code that has no non-raising version'). Haiku-2's `Map.get(user, :name) || "there"` (line 102) is 'violated' under 'Read required keys...' ('read struct fields with `user.name` or a pattern'). Haiku-1's line 56 `opts[:notify] and not opts[:silent]` is 'violated' under 'Use `and`, `or`, `not`...' although it reported line 21: the rule keeps `&&`/`!` for values that may be nil, and the line makes `import_user(params)` raise.

Judgment calls on 'reported': haiku-1 finding 9 ('Nested `if` and `&&` for control flow ... `if is_binary(email) && age >= 18` mixes boolean operators and nests a `case` inside an `if`/`else`. A `with` chain flattens this') counts for both the nesting and the line 21 `&&`; opus-1 finding 16 counts for line 12; opus-1 finding 11 counts for the changeset although its code keeps the bare struct on purpose (the rule is still violated); opus-1 lines 36,39 do not count, since the specific reasons appear only under 'Behaviour changes callers must know about' (review.md line 133); sonnet-1 finding 3's 'return tagged errors' does not count for lines 36,39, since it names no distinct reasons and the code keeps `{:error, :invalid}`; sonnet-2 finding 12's 'drop one of the two flags' counts for the overlapping options; haiku-2 finding 8 counts for the spawn ('the process is not tracked ... a `Task.Supervisor` is better') though its code uses `Task.start/1`.

Must-not-report lines: sonnet-1 finding 10 and sonnet-2 finding 12 say to use `and`/`not` for line 26's `opts[:notify] && !opts[:silent]`, so each is a false positive. Haiku-2 finding 12 says line 26's `&&`/`!` are correct, so it is not one. No run reports line 11 or line 19's access or `||` (opus-1 finding 17, sonnet-1 finding 5 and sonnet-2 finding 5 are about blank nicknames).
findings_name_rule_and_quote is 'partly' for every run: findings quote code fragments (opus-1 also gives input line numbers), but no finding names a rule.
Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex.

Format check: the improved module (one elixir block in each review.md) extracted to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-idiomatic-elixir-skill/1e47a876-c0bc-571c-a7e7-3b8d4cc5c310/scratchpad/grading/code-review-baseline/baseline-<run>.ex; result.json has no format_ok field, so mix format --check-formatted (Elixir 1.20.4) was run there and exits 0 for all five.
